title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
authors: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain, Pieter Abbeel
summary: Shows that a simple noise-prediction objective trains diffusion models that rival GANs on image quality.
takeaways: Predicting the noise is easier to optimise than predicting the image.
The simplified loss drops the weighting term and works better in practice.
Sampling needs about 1000 steps, which is the main cost.

title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
authors: Robin Rombach, Andreas Blattmann, Dominik Lorenz, Patrick Esser, Björn Ommer
summary: Runs diffusion in the latent space of a pretrained autoencoder, cutting compute while keeping detail.
takeaways: Compress first, diffuse second: most pixels carry perceptual detail the diffusion model does not need to learn.
Cross-attention gives flexible conditioning on text or other inputs.

title: Grad-CAM: Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-based Localization
authors: Ramprasaath R. Selvaraju, Michael Cogswell, Abhishek Das, Ramakrishna Vedantam, Devi Parikh, Dhruv Batra
summary: Uses gradients flowing into the last convolutional layer to highlight image regions behind a prediction.
takeaways: Works on many CNN architectures without retraining.
A heatmap shows where the model looked, not necessarily why it decided.
